_serves_note: canvas.html fetches /canvas-license.json and this provider answers it, returning {} when no key file is present. It is not an /api/ path, so it matched no serves prefix and never reached the provider at all — an undeclared byte route falls through to the SDK runtime. Declaring it is what makes the provider's answer reachable. tldraw licensing itself is bring-your-own: a box that carries app/canvas-license.json is keyed, and one that does not shows a header link to tldraw.dev. Neither state is a defect and neither is this route's concern.
_verbs_note: THIS LIST IS DELIBERATELY 36 OF THE 43 VERBS THIS FILE ANSWERS, AND THE GAP IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Withheld: /api/note, /api/note/done, /api/note/flush, /api/note/reconciled, /api/receivers, /api/reveal-file, /api/shell-mtime. The first four reach `execFile("rig", ["queue","create", ...])` — live in export-server.mjs — so declaring them would let a Studio surface inject work into the agent system that runs the box. /api/reveal-file runs `open -R`, which is macOS Finder and meaningless on the Linux boxes this ships to. THE CHOICE IS BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING, WHICH IS THE POINT: on a box running more than one provider these seven ALREADY do not route, because no app declares them and the runtime's single-provider fallback needs exactly one provider. Declaring them here would ENABLE something currently unreachable — a policy change smuggled inside a format migration. A migration changes where a fact is written, never what the product does. Whether these verbs SHOULD be exposed is a live product question and this file is not where it gets decided.
_seeds_note: First-run seeding moved off a hardcoded path onto a provider declaration in the SDK tooling. Until this file existed the boot tool carried THIS provider's file name, module export and marker as literals, which made first-run seeding a video-studio feature no other kind of studio could use. `marker` is the file whose presence means already-seeded; seeding runs only into an absent or empty directory, so a directory with contents and no marker is somebody's data and the box refuses rather than seeding over it.
_seeds_upstream_defect: 🟢 RESOLVED (fixed upstream in the SDK tooling) — KEPT RATHER THAN DELETED, because the reasoning is why the declaration is shaped this way and a future reader would otherwise re-litigate it. WHAT WAS WRONG: compose-rail.mjs copied only run/serves/verbs off a provider.json, so the top-level `seeds` this contract documents never reached studio.mjs, which read `spec.run?.seeds ?? spec.seeds`. Measured both ways on one boot: top level gave the LEGACY hardcoded-path warning and seeded via fallback; the identical block under `run.seeds` gave 'seeded (declared by …)'. I SHIPPED THE DOCUMENTED SHAPE ANYWAY and did not nest, because nesting works today and ships a second undocumented shape for one fact — the defect this migration removes. THAT CALL IS NOW LOAD-BEARING: the fix makes the reader accept ONLY the documented shape, so `run.seeds` no longer works at all. Nesting would have shipped a manifest that broke on their next commit. RE-MEASURED under 58130c4: 'seeded: <root> (declared by @openrig/studio-video)', no legacy warning, timeline.json created. THE DIAGNOSIS WORTH KEEPING: a PERMISSIVE READER HID A BROKEN WRITER. `a ?? b` tolerated two shapes without anyone checking which one the composer could actually produce, so NEITHER branch could fire and the failure waited for a real migration to surface it. A reader that accepted only the documented shape would have failed the first time anyone declared one.
_why_this_file_exists: Three apps — canvas, media-manager and mini-nle — each carried a byte-identical copy of the run spec above, because an app was the only place the format let you write it. Three copies of one fact drift, and the drift is silent: the same shape already cost this project live rig state when retiring the AGENTS app deleted the only declaration of {{state}} and a deployed box's landing page served an invented rig under a green live signal. The provider is authoritative about how to start itself; an app is a client that names it.
